topic: Deletion safety model for a system cleaner: dry-run default, trash vs permanent delete, age thresholds, open-file checks, symlink escape prevention, path canonicalization
rules: Dry-run is the default for any delete path: clean without an explicit apply flag only scans and reports (BleachBit preview / docker confirm pattern).
Trash/Recycle Bin is the default delete method; permanent unlink is opt-in only, never the silent default (trash-cli / FreeDesktop recoverability).
Permanent mass delete requires a second confirmation barrier (typed phrase or interactive confirm); --yes alone is insufficient.
Per-rule minimum age thresholds gate sticky regenerable junk; global override is allowed, but age 0 only disables the age gate, not other safety checks (docker until= filters).
Never-touch paths (user data roots, secrets, system trees, filesystem roots) always override rules and are re-checked at delete time.
Authorize only after path canonicalization (canonicalize if exists, else lexical normalize of . and ..); failed normalization means refuse.
Every candidate must stay under its rule root after normalization; refuse symlink escapes that leave the allowed root.
Do not force-delete open or locked files by default: skip, report, and continue (best-effort EBUSY / sharing-violation handling).
High-blast categories (named volumes, archives, package stores, OS restore points) are report-only unless a separate, warned opt-in path is used (docker volumes excluded from default system prune).
Medium/high-risk rules and shred/wipe modes are disabled by default and never auto-enabled for a max clean score.
Revalidate existence, never-touch, and root containment between scan and delete; failures are skipped with logged reasons.
Delete deepest paths first; continue on per-item errors and surface them; report method (dry-run|trash|permanent), counts, bytes, and skips with no silent blocked deletes.
Core junk cleaning must not require root/admin; privileged system cleaning is out of the default MVP path.
Secure overwrite/shred is out of MVP default backends and, if added later, still inherits dry-run, trash preference, never-touch, and confirm rules.
must_have: Dry-run default on clean (no disk mutation without explicit apply)
Explicit apply flag (--yes or equivalent) to perform deletes
Trash-first delete via OS Trash / FreeDesktop Trash / Recycle Bin
Permanent delete only with second-factor confirm (typed phrase)
Per-rule min_age_days plus optional global age override
Hard never-touch denylist enforced at scan and delete
Path canonicalize with lexical fallback and fail-closed on error
Symlink escape guard: candidate must stay under rule root after normalize
Skip/report locked or in-use files instead of force-delete
report_only support for dangerous rule categories
Delete-time safety revalidation (TOCTOU harden)
Auditable report (human + JSON) of method, freed bytes, skips, and errors
anti_patterns: Permanent unlink (rm-style) as the default cleaner action
Any clean mode that deletes without a prior dry-run/preview path
Following symlinks out of rule roots into home or system trees
Letting YAML/rules override never-touch or filesystem-root protections
Authorizing deletes on non-canonical paths (../, unresolved links, mixed roots)
Including volumes, package stores, or archives in default prune without opt-in
Force-deleting open databases or live app data and reporting success
Auto-enabling high-risk, shred, or wipe modes for aggressive cleaning
Silently ignoring blocked or failed paths without error counters
Scareware health scores or dark patterns that push permanent mass deletes

topic: Rule engine design: YAML/JSON clean rules (BleachBit-style), allowlist/denylist, per-app plugins, versioned rule packs
rules: Rules are declarative data only (YAML primary, JSON same schema); no shell/process/code execution inside rule files in core.
Every rule has a stable unique id, human name/description, category, risk, platform, and explicit path templates; scan/clean must attribute every path to a rule id and pack.
Path templates expand env/XDG/Windows variables; refuse filesystem roots and bare home as rule roots; enforce post-normalize stay-under-root against symlink escape.
Risk is binding: low may default on; medium/high default off; report_only never deletes on the normal clean path even with --yes.
Age (min_age_days), include/exclude globs, max_depth, and delete_mode (prefer contents over path) are first-class match constraints.
Hard denylist in code (Documents/Desktop/Downloads, keys/mail, system trees, home, roots) always wins; user path denylist wins over rules; user allowlist cannot override hard denylist or report_only.
Per-app targets are separate rules in named packs (apps/dev/os); browser rules are cache-only by default; cookies/logins/history stay off or high-risk separate rules.
Packs are versioned (pack_version + schema_version); load order is shipped then site then user with documented id override; refuse silent misparse of unknown schema.
Special cleaners (docker prune, package managers, registry, sqlite vacuum) are plugins with the same candidate model; default docker-like volume/data stores stay report-only or explicit opt-in.
Default delete semantics are trash/restore-friendly (trash-cli/FreeDesktop style); permanent delete is explicit; shred/overwrite is out of MVP.
Dry-run/preview and path transparency are required before destructive clean; no hidden rule expansion beyond user-selected categories/ids.
must_have: YAML rule packs with id, category, risk, platform, paths, globs, min_age_days, delete_mode, default_enabled, report_only
Multi-dir load: bundled packs plus user rules directory with documented id override
Unix and Windows path template expansion ($HOME, $XDG_*, %LOCALAPPDATA%, etc.)
Hard never-touch denylist enforced on every match after normalize
Dry-run scan report mapping path/size/risk to rule id
Trash-backed clean with confirmation; report_only never deletes
Risk gates: medium/high off by default
CLI list rules, show rule, list categories, doctor (sources/packs)
pack_version and schema_version surfaced in doctor/version output
Include/exclude globs and max_depth for precise app/browser rules
User path denylist config that always excludes matches
Platform filtering so only host-matching rules activate
anti_patterns: Never ship or accept rules that wipe whole home, Documents, Desktop, or Downloads without hard blocks
Never execute shell/binaries from rule YAML/JSON in the core engine
Never default-enable cookies, logins, mail, SSH, or key material cleaning
Never prune Docker volumes or shared package stores (e.g. pnpm store) except report-only or ultra-explicit plugin flags
Never let config disable the hard denylist or quietly force-delete report_only rules
Never unbounded-walk entire home/disk as a built-in pack rule
Never auto-apply unauthenticated remote rule-pack updates into deletes
Never hide which rule matched a deleted path
Never make secure multi-pass wipe the default clean path
Never use scareware scores, fake health meters, or registry cleaning as default value

topic: CLI UX for cleaners: subcommands, table/JSON, exit codes, CI, progress
rules: Verbs only: scan (read-only), clean (mutate), doctor (self-check), rules list|show; same filters on scan and clean so scan is a true dry-run of clean.
scan never mutates; clean defaults to dry-run and only deletes with explicit --yes (BleachBit preview vs clean).
Human default is table; machines use -o json|--format json on every data-bearing command.
JSON is complete and stable (full findings, totals, skipped roots, rule ids); table may truncate via --limit; schema additive only.
Stdout holds table/JSON payload; stderr holds progress, warnings, prompts, and errors so pipes to jq stay clean.
Exit codes are public API: 0 success (including empty scan), 1 operational/partial failure, 2 usage/config error; document in --help.
Noninteractive when not a TTY, --yes/--non-interactive, or CI: no prompts, no TTY-only spinners; refuse destructive clean if confirmation missing (fail closed, never hang).
Risk-matched confirmation: Trash delete needs --yes; permanent mass delete needs a second gate (confirm phrase); never treat piped input as yes.
Progress only on interactive TTY stderr; quiet under --json/non-TTY; SIGINT aborts with partial report and non-success if work incomplete.
rules and doctor are first-class, offline, same output formats so operators audit CI targets before --yes.
must_have: Subcommands: scan, clean, doctor, rules list|show
Shared filters: category, min-age, include high-risk
Table: size, path, category, risk, rule id, category summary, truncate + hint
JSON on stdout for scan, clean, doctor, rules
clean dry-run default; --yes applies; Trash default; permanent + hard confirm
CI/non-TTY: no hang; refuse clean without --yes
TTY progress on long runs; silent under JSON/non-TTY
Documented exit codes; 0 empty success; nonzero on real failure
Actionable stderr errors with next step (e.g. pass --yes)
anti_patterns: Default-on or surprise delete without scan/preview
Interactive y/N with no --yes/--force for scripts
Progress, color, or logs mixed into JSON stdout
Different filter meaning between scan and clean
Exit 0 when some deletes failed
GUI-only presets required for headless clean
Opaque deletes without path and rule id
Empty stdin or pipe treated as confirmation
Unbounded table of millions of paths without limit/JSON escape

topic: Legal/ethical product rules: no scareware, no forced upsell, honest sizes, accessible deletion logs
rules: Never invent PC dirty/health/threat scores or urgency not backed by concrete reclaimable paths.
Present scan results as facts only: bytes, paths, categories, risk, and rule IDs.
Default flow is preview then explicit user choice then confirm then clean; no silent first-run bulk delete.
Dry-run/preview is the safe default; never delete without preview or an explicit noninteractive consent flag.
Report measured reclaimable size on scan and attempted vs actually freed after clean; explain hard links, sparse files, and permission skips.
Never inflate sizes via double-counting, marketing up to claims, or non-deleted optimization theater.
Rule labels must match deleted content (e.g. logs must not wipe caches or settings).
Core clean path must work without accounts, licenses, nag screens, or paid unlock for real delete.
Every clean produces an accessible audit log or machine-readable report of deleted, failed, and skipped items with timestamps, sizes, and rule IDs.
Default to trash/recoverable delete; permanent delete only via explicit harder-to-reach option.
Interactive sessions confirm before delete; noninteractive requires explicit --yes/--force, never implied by scan.
No dark-pattern consent: no pre-checked high-risk wipe-all, buried extras, or fake progress inventing work.
Do not overclaim 100% safe, legal compliance theater, or malware removal unless those features truly exist and are separate.
No phone-home of path inventories or machine fingerprints without clear opt-in telemetry; default is no telemetry.
Report partial cleans honestly (permission denied, in-use files); never claim full success when results were partial.
must_have: Preview/dry-run scan listing paths, categories, risk, and byte sizes before any delete
Clean command or flag separate from scan with interactive confirmation
Accurate per-finding, per-category, and total size aggregation
Post-clean summary with deleted count, bytes removed, and failures/skips with reasons
Persistent or exportable deletion log (human-readable and JSON) of what was deleted
Trash-first delete path with permanent delete only via explicit flag
Accurate rule labels/descriptions shipped with rule packs
No health score or scare UI in CLI output or documentation
Opt-in noninteractive mode that still writes full deletion logs
Medium/high-risk categories off by default until user opts in
Public docs of each category and what defaults never touch
anti_patterns: Fake Your PC is N% dirty/infected gauges to drive action
Auto-clean on install, login, or schedule without prior user configuration
Freemium wall: free scan but paid delete or paid access to deletion logs
Blocking or mid-clean upsells to finish cleaning
Inflating reclaimable space with free space, other volumes, or unselected categories
Registry fix, startup optimizer, or RAM booster dressed as junk cleaning
Bundled PUPs, browser hijackers, or default-on affiliate installers
Deleting settings, passwords, or cookies under a cache or junk label
Hiding or paywalling deletion logs so users cannot audit what was removed
Reporting cleaned when files were only skipped or silently moved without saying so
